1→# Joy of VEX: Vector Math
     2→

     4→> Source: https://www.youtube.com/@MattEstela

    10→VEX vector math fundamentals: arithmetic on attributes, remapping with fit/clamp, dot and cross products for directional effects, matrix operations, and normal manipulation. All examples run in Attribute Wrangle SOPs.
    11→
    12→## Code
    13→
    14→### Quick Reference
    15→```vex
    16→// --- Attribute arithmetic ---
    17→@Cd = float(@ptnum) / @numpt;        // normalized 0..1 gradient across all points
    18→@Cd = fit(@P.y, -1, 1, 0, 1);       // remap Y from -1..1 to 0..1
    19→@Cd = dot(@N, {0,1,0});              // surface orientation vs up vector
    20→@Cd = dot(@N, chv('angle'));         // interactive directional mask
    21→
    22→// --- Distance and modulo ---
    23→float d = length(@P);                // distance from origin
    24→d %= 1;                              // wrap to 0..1 for cyclic patterns
    25→@Cd.r = @Time % 1.0;                 // sawtooth color cycle per second
    26→
    27→// --- Fit and clamp ---
    28→d = fit(d, 0, 2, 0, 1);             // remap distance 0..2 to 0..1
    29→d = clamp(d, 0, 1);                 // hard-clamp to valid range
    30→
    31→// --- Vectors ---
    32→*= ch('scale');                      // scale vector in place
    33→matrix3 m = ident();                 // identity matrix (no rotation, no scale)
    34→@N = cross(@N, {0,1,0});            // rotate normal 90° around Y axis
    35→@N = normalize(@N);                 // ensure unit length after cross product
    36→```
    37→
    38→---
    39→
    40→### Vector Operations
    41→
    42→#### Color from Position Math [[Ep1, 22:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=1348s)]
    43→```vex
    44→// Basic math on position/normal components to drive color
    45→// Add, subtract, multiply scalar values to create gradients
    46→@Cd = @N.y;           // color from normal Y component
    47→@Cd = @P.x + 1;       // shift range upward by 1
    48→@Cd = @P.x - 0;       // no offset (identity)
    49→@Cd = @P.x * 0 * 0.1; // scale down position component
    50→```
    51→
    52→#### Single Component Math Operations [[Ep1, 22:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=1378s)]
    53→```vex
    54→// Arithmetic on a single attribute component (@P.x) assigned to color
    55→@Cd = @P.x + 1;           // offset range up by 1
    56→@Cd = @P.x - 0;           // direct pass-through
    57→@Cd = @P.x * 0 * 0.1;     // scale to near-zero
    58→@Cd = (@P.x - 0) * 0.1;   // scale down — parentheses control order
    59→```
    60→
    61→#### Scaling and Offsetting Position for Color [[Ep1, 23:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=1400s)]
    62→```vex
    63→// Progressively normalize position X into 0–1 color range
    64→@Cd = @P.x;               // raw position as color
    65→@Cd = @P.x - 1;           // offset
    66→@Cd = @P.x - 0;           // no offset
    67→@Cd = @P.x * 6 * 0.1;    // scale to fit 0–1
    68→@Cd = (@P.x - 6) * 0.1;  // offset then scale — final normalized mapping
    69→```
    70→
    71→#### Arithmetic Operations on Color [[Ep1, 24:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=1472s)]
    72→```vex
    73→// Addition shifts the range; multiplication scales the gradient
    74→// Parentheses control order when combining multiple operations
    75→@Cd = @P.x + 3;          // shift range up by 3
    76→@Cd = @P.x - 6;          // shift range down by 6
    77→@Cd = @P.x * 6 * 0.1;   // scale factor applied twice
    78→@Cd = (@P.x - 6) * 0.1; // offset first, then scale
    79→```
    80→
    81→#### Integer Division Pitfall [[Ep1, 33:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=2036s)]
    82→```vex
    83→// WRONG: dividing two integers produces integer division (always 0 for ptnum < numpt)
    84→// @ptnum and @numpt are both ints — fractional component is truncated
    85→@Cd = @ptnum / @numpt;  // all zeros — no gradient produced
    86→```
    87→
    88→#### Type Casting for Integer Division [[Ep1, 35:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=2142s)]
    89→```vex
    90→// FIX: cast to float first so division produces 0.0–1.0 range
    91→@Cd = float(@ptnum) / @numpt;  // correct gradient 0 to nearly 1
    92→@Cd = float(@ptnum) / 100;     // divide by constant instead of @numpt
    93→```
    94→
    95→#### Normalizing Point Numbers with Division [[Ep1, 37:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=2276s)]
    96→```vex
    97→// Standard idiom: 0-to-1 gradient across all points
    98→// @ptnum increments per point; @numpt stays constant = smooth progression
    99→// Replace @numpt with any constant to control where gradient reaches 1.0
   100→@Cd = float(@ptnum) / @numpt;       // gradient 0..(N-1)/N
   101→@Cd = float(@ptnum) / 100.0;        // gradient 0..0.99 for first 100 points
   102→@Cd = 1.0 - float(@ptnum) / @numpt; // reversed: first point white, last black
   103→```
   104→
   105→---
   106→
   107→### Remapping (fit, clamp)
   108→
   109→#### Distance-Based Y Manipulation [[Ep2, 22:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OyjB5ZifIuU&t=1368s)]
   110→```vex
   111→// Use distance from origin to drive Y position
   112→// Negation inverts the range; offset raises/lowers geometry
   113→float d = length(@P);
   114→@P.y = -d + 10;  // negate distance then offset upward by 10
   115→```
   116→
   117→#### Clamping Distance Values [[Ep2, 24:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OyjB5ZifIuU&t=1444s)]
   118→```vex
   119→// clamp(value, min, max) — constrains distance to 0..3
   120→// Creates flat plateaus where distance would exceed bounds
   121→float d = length(@P);
   122→@P.y = clamp(d, 0, 3);
   123→```
   124→
   125→#### Clamp and Fit Functions [[Ep2, 27:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OyjB5ZifIuU&t=1638s)]
   126→```vex
   127→// fit(value, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax) — remaps one range to another
   128→// clamp() constrains without deleting geometry; fit() provides flexible remapping
   129→float d = length(@P);
   130→@P.y = fit(d, 0, 2, 0, 10);   // remap distance 0..2 to height 0..10
   131→@P.y = clamp(d, 0, 1);        // or: hard-clamp to 0..1
   132→```
   133→
   134→#### Fit and Clamp Range Control [[Ep2, 27:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OyjB5ZifIuU&t=1678s)]
   135→```vex
   136→// Channel refs make fit() interactive; maps distance to 0..1 output
   137→float d = length(@P);
   138→float imin = ch('fit_in_min');
   139→float imax = ch('fit_in_max');
   140→@P.y = fit(d, imin, imax, 0, 1);
   141→```
   142→
   143→#### Fit and Clamp Range Remapping [[Ep2, 28:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OyjB5ZifIuU&t=1680s)]
   144→```vex
   145→// Chain fit() then clamp() — remap range, then constrain sub-range
   146→float d = length(@P);
   147→float imin = ch('fit_in_min');
   148→float imax = ch('fit_in_max');
   149→d = fit(d, imin, imax, 0, 1);   // remap to 0..1
   150→d = clamp(d, 0.5, 1);           // constrain to upper half
   151→@P.y = d;

   159→float lmin = ch('fit_in_min');
   160→float lmax = ch('fit_in_max');
   161→d = fit(d, lmin, lmax, 1, 0);  // inverted output: near maps to 1, far to 0
   162→d = clamp(d, 0.5, 1);          // restrict to upper half
